memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Jacob's sons did as he had commanded them: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought along with the field as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite. After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and all the others who had gone with him to bury his father." — Gen 50:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Jacob's sons did as he had commanded them." Twelve brothers, who once could not agree on anything and nearly destroyed each other, carrying their father home together.

They buried him in the cave at Machpelah, alongside Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah. Four generations in a single field — the only ground in Canaan the family actually owned.

That cave is a quiet monument to faith. Abraham bought it with cash while God's promise of the whole land was still entirely unfulfilled. Every burial there was an act of trust: we belong to this land because God said so, even though we do not possess it yet.

And then Joseph returns to Egypt. The promise is not complete. Four hundred years of waiting lie ahead, most of it hard.

Faith often looks like this — doing what has been asked, honouring what has been promised, and then going back to ordinary life with the fulfilment still ahead. Hebrews says these people were still living by faith when they died, without having received the things promised (Heb 11:13).

Faithfulness in the waiting is faith at its most real.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God asked of you that you need simply to do?
2. Are you able to be faithful while the promise is still unfulfilled?
3. What are you waiting on that requires trust rather than sight?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me be faithful in the waiting, doing what You have asked while Your promises are still ahead of me. Thank You that You always keep Your word. Amen.
